sources.citation: game-design: an adjustable torque screwdriver drives a screw and slips at its setting, so it has drive and torque, with no conductor size limit. The torque a terminal needs comes from the device's own marking (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D), cited by number), never from a torque table.

game-design: unverified product-class figures, for electrical-realism-reviewer to check. ISO 6789-1 (cited by number) classes adjustable torque screwdrivers as setting tools, and makers commonly state a permissible deviation of plus or minus 6 % of the setting, verified from 20 % to 100 % of the maximum. A 1-5 N·m range keeps the minimum at 20 % of the maximum and reaches the 4 N·m this game's branch-breaker and stand-in service screws are marked with; the 0.5 N·m DIN supply terminals are below it (a plain screwdriver lands them until a low-range driver is added).
